audit.why: Emerald+ 49.86% over 712 games — the only losing matchup in this slice, and the entry's upbeat "you dictate the lane" framing sits oddly against it. Number itself is right.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry states twice that Galio "has no dash" — spikes[1] ("Galio has no dash to escape your range") and whys[3] ("he has no dash to escape your point-and-click lockdown").
audit.why: Justice Punch is a dash: "Galio will briefly step back and charge, knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters", 650 range, 11/10/9/8/7s. It is flagged dash in the kit. The entire "he cannot escape the lockdown" plan is built on a mobility gap that does not exist, and the full layer contradicts the content layer by correctly calling Justice Punch "His dash + knockup engage".
audit.corrected: Both lines now name Justice Punch, its 650 range and its 11s rank-1 cooldown, and tell the player to bait it before committing.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says "his MR stacking is largely wasted against your physical-skewed kit" and whys[6] repeats "his MR stack does not neutralise your physical-skewed empowered autos".
audit.why: Devour explicitly "deal[s] magic damage if they are an enemy" per the kit. Galio's MR is therefore directly relevant, and the entry contradicts itself — wants.foe[1] already says "MR itemisation blunts your own AP-scaling empowered Devour damage". Telling a player that a tank's MR is wasted against them is exactly the kind of error that makes them force a losing trade.
audit.corrected: Both lines corrected to say his MR does cut Devour, and to route the win through Sunfire burn and lockdown instead of the swallow's damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the content layer never names a single Galio ability — it says "his Q", "his W taunt", "his R" throughout.
audit.why: Colossal Smash, Winds of War, Shield of Durand, Justice Punch and Hero's Entrance are all absent, so the reader cannot map advice onto what they see on the loading screen. Naming them also lets the real numbers in: Winds of War is 825 range against Tongue Lash's 900 (the poke gap the entry gestures at), and Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1 with a 4000-unit range.
audit.corrected: Ability names and the range/cooldown figures added across early, mid, late, spikes[1], spikes[2], whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], wants.you[0], wants.foe[0] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreement: content win[] gives Level 1 to Tahm Kench and Levels 4-5 to Tahm Kench, while full.phases[0].side and full.phases[3].side both say "Skill"; content gives Level 6 to Galio and full.phases[4].side says "Skill".
audit.why: Same chart, two renderings, three stages out of seven disagree. Not edited — I have no kit-level basis for choosing a side, and guessing would put a fabricated power shift in front of a player.

edits.before: Tongue Lash's range is longer than Galio's Q footprint, so step up, land Q to start stacking An Acquired Taste, and immediately step back before his passive magic-damage auto procs. Thick Skin converts that auto into grey health you will heal back off-combat, so don't panic-burn E to shield it — save the active for when you commit to a full trade. Galio level 1 has nothing to close the gap on you; he will try to match your poke and shove early. Don't let him push you under tower without landing at least one stun setup — the 3-stack Q stun is your level-2 threat and he knows it.
edits.after: Tongue Lash reaches 900 against Winds of War's 825, so step up, land Q to start stacking An Acquired Taste, and step back before Colossal Smash resets his auto into you. Thick Skin converts that auto into grey health you will heal back off-combat, so don't panic-burn E to shield it — save the active for when you commit to a full trade. Justice Punch is not up at level 1, so he cannot close on you; he will try to match your poke and shove early. Don't let him push you under tower without landing at least one stun setup — the 3-stack Q stun is your level-2 threat and he knows it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your window to extract real value: Galio's W taunt has a slow wind-up, so if you open with Tongue Lash from stun range he can't react in time to catch your Devour in the taunt. The pattern is Q to stun, then Devour immediately — he is removed from the fight for the duration and takes empowered damage. His Q poke is annoying but not lethal, and your Thick Skin sustain means he is not winning the attrition war. At 6 his R changes the equation entirely — when it is up, trade short, stack up, and let the threat of your Devour combo force him to play reactively rather than proactively. When his R is on cooldown you still dictate the lane.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your window to extract real value: Shield of Durand charges visibly before it taunts, so if you open with Tongue Lash from stun range he can't react in time to catch your Devour in the taunt. The pattern is Q for the third stack, then Devour immediately — a Q at 3 stuns instead and consumes exactly what Devour needs. His Q poke is annoying but not lethal, and your Thick Skin sustain means he is not winning the attrition war. At 6 Hero's Entrance changes the equation, 180s at rank 1 — when it is up, trade short, stack up, and let the threat of your Devour combo force him to play reactively rather than proactively. On that cooldown you still dictate the lane.

edits.before: First item onwards you become extremely difficult to kill in sustained fights: Heartsteel or Sunfire combined with Thick Skin grey-health recovery means Galio's repeated magic-damage passive autos and Q casts barely move your health bar across a long trade. He cannot burst you, his MR stacking is largely wasted against your physical-skewed kit, and your Devour's point-and-click removal is fully online. Play around his R cooldown in side lane and teamfights — the moment his global is down, force a skirmish. At 2+ items you are a near-unkillable frontliner and his peel or engage is the only thing he brings to the fight; deny him the flank angle and your team dismantles him.
edits.after: First item onwards you become extremely difficult to kill in sustained fights: Heartsteel or Sunfire combined with Thick Skin grey-health recovery means Colossal Smash procs and Winds of War casts barely move your health bar across a long trade. He cannot burst you, but his MR does blunt Devour, because that damage is magic, so win it on Sunfire burn and lockdown, not the swallow. Play around Hero's Entrance in side lane and teamfights — the moment his global is down, force a skirmish. At 2+ items you are a near-unkillable frontliner and his peel or engage is the only thing he brings to the fight; deny him the flank angle and your team dismantles him.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks into Devour is online cleanly — Galio has no dash to escape your range once the stun lands, and his W taunt is too slow to preempt the combo.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks into Devour is online cleanly — but Justice Punch is a 650-range dash on an 11s rank-1 cooldown — swallow him after he spends it, not before.

edits.before: Galio's R gives him global team-fight presence and a shield that soaks your grey-health swing; respect his ultimate timer and stop trading into his W taunt when his R is up.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance shields his whole team on landing and knocks you up; respect its 180s rank-1 timer and stop trading into Shield of Durand's taunt while the ult is up.

edits.before: Your empowered Devour stun combo is live but so is his W taunt window — the lane is a skill-matchup of who lands their crowd control first.
edits.after: Devour is live at three stacks but so is Shield of Durand's taunt — the lane is a skill-matchup of who lands their crowd control first.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks into the stun-Devour combo punishes any Galio overextension cleanly; he has no dash to escape your point-and-click lockdown.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks into the stun-Devour combo punishes any Galio overextension cleanly; Justice Punch is his 650-range dash out — bait it first.

edits.before: His R comes online and gives him global presence that swings teamfights elsewhere; you cannot follow and his W taunt makes extended 1v1 trades punishing if you walk into it.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance reaches 4000 units at rank 1 and swings fights you cannot reach; Shield of Durand's taunt makes extended 1v1 trades punishing if you walk into it.

edits.before: You remain a durable frontliner who removes him from teamfights with Devour; his MR stack does not neutralise your physical-skewed empowered autos and Sunfire burn at full build.
edits.after: You remain a durable frontliner who removes him from teamfights with Devour; his MR does cut Devour's magic damage, so win it on Sunfire burn and lockdown, not the swallow.

edits.before: Land Tongue Lash to stack An Acquired Taste and punish Galio's Q cast animation before he can step back
edits.after: Land Tongue Lash to stack An Acquired Taste and punish the Winds of War cast before he can step back

edits.before: Stack his W taunt to absorb your Devour and force you to either cancel or eat the taunt duration
edits.after: Hold Shield of Durand to absorb your Devour and force you to either cancel or eat the taunt duration

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash + knockup engage. Punish him when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — 650-range dash + knockup, 11s at rank 1. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Weakest entry in the slice and it got the most work: 49.86% is a losing matchup written up as a winning one, built on two flat factual errors (Galio "has no dash", and his MR being "wasted" against a kit whose ultimate deals magic damage). I did NOT act on the _missing-interactions line "Galio can cut your retreat with Justice Punch (E)... hold Flash for the wall" — it is derived from a `terrain` flag on Justice Punch that looks like a bad derivation, since Justice Punch creates no terrain. Worth checking the flag generator.
